theory.intro: When you know two sides and a non-included angle (an SSA triangle), the sine rule can give **two** possible triangles. Because $\sin\theta=\sin(180^{\circ}-\theta)$, the calculator's acute answer $\theta$ and its obtuse partner $180^{\circ}-\theta$ can **both** fit. Always find both, then check each: the obtuse angle is valid only if it still leaves room in the triangle's $180^{\circ}$ angle sum.
facts: The sine rule $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{a}=\dfrac{\sin A}{b}$ gives $\sin\theta$; since $\sin\theta=\sin(180^{\circ}-\theta)$ there may be an acute **and** an obtuse solution.
Find the acute angle $\theta=\sin^{-1}(\ldots)$, then its obtuse partner $\theta'=180^{\circ}-\theta$.
The obtuse solution $\theta'$ is valid only if $\theta'+(\text{given angle})<180^{\circ}$; otherwise the angle sum would exceed $180^{\circ}$ and it is rejected.
If the given angle is already obtuse, there is only **one** solution — a triangle can have at most one obtuse angle.
If the sine rule gives $\sin\theta>1$, no triangle exists.
You can predict the number of triangles: with given angle $A$ and sides $a$, $b$, two triangles occur when $b\sin A<a<b$.
steps: Use the sine rule to find the acute angle theta
Find the obtuse partner 180 degrees minus theta
Add each possible angle to the given angle and reject any whose sum reaches 180 degrees
State all valid values of the angle

foundation.question_text: Two triangles have sides $8$ and $6$, where the angle opposite the $6$ side is $40^{\circ}$. Find, in each case, the size of the angle $\theta$ opposite the $8$ side, correct to $2$ decimal places.
foundation.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{8}=\dfrac{\sin 40^{\circ}}{6}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{8\sin 40^{\circ}}{6}$
$\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{8\sin 40^{\circ}}{6}\right)$
$=58.99^{\circ}$
The obtuse partner is $180^{\circ}-58.99^{\circ}=121.01^{\circ}$.
Check: $121.01^{\circ}+40^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$, so both are valid.
$\theta=58.99^{\circ}$ or $121.01^{\circ}$

$=61.85^{\circ}$

development.question_text: In triangle $ABC$, side $a=13$ is opposite $\angle A=54^{\circ}$ and side $b=7$ is opposite $\angle B$. Find $\angle B$ and explain why only one solution is possible. Answer to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\sin B}{7}=\dfrac{\sin 54^{\circ}}{13}$
$\sin B=\dfrac{7\sin 54^{\circ}}{13}$
$B=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{7\sin 54^{\circ}}{13}\right)$
$=25.83^{\circ}$
The obtuse partner $180^{\circ}-25.83^{\circ}=154.17^{\circ}$ gives $154.17^{\circ}+54^{\circ}=208.17^{\circ}>180^{\circ}$, so it is rejected.
$\angle B=25.83^{\circ}$ only

$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{5}=\dfrac{\sin 105^{\circ}}{9}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{5\sin 105^{\circ}}{9}$
$\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5\sin 105^{\circ}}{9}\right)$
$=32.45^{\circ}$
The given angle $105^{\circ}$ is obtuse, so the other angles are acute — there is only one solution.
$\theta=32.45^{\circ}$

development.question_text: Two triangles have sides $10$ and $7$, where the angle opposite the $7$ side is $40^{\circ}$. For each triangle, find the third angle (the angle opposite the unknown side), correct to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{10}=\dfrac{\sin 40^{\circ}}{7}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{10\sin 40^{\circ}}{7}$
$\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{10\sin 40^{\circ}}{7}\right)$
$=66.67^{\circ}$
The obtuse partner is $180^{\circ}-66.67^{\circ}=113.33^{\circ}$; both are valid since $113.33^{\circ}+40^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$.
Acute case: third angle $=180^{\circ}-40^{\circ}-66.67^{\circ}=73.33^{\circ}$.
Obtuse case: third angle $=180^{\circ}-40^{\circ}-113.33^{\circ}=26.67^{\circ}$.

development.question_text: A triangle is claimed to have sides $8$ and $5$, where the angle opposite the $5$ side is $40^{\circ}$. Find the angle $\theta$ opposite the $8$ side, or explain why no such triangle exists.
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{8}=\dfrac{\sin 40^{\circ}}{5}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{8\sin 40^{\circ}}{5}$
$=1.03$
Since $\sin\theta$ cannot exceed $1$, no such triangle exists.

mastery.question_text: In triangle $PQR$, $p=7$ is opposite $\angle P=45^{\circ}$ and $q=9$ is opposite $\angle Q$. Find both possible sizes of $\angle Q$, and the corresponding length of side $r$, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\sin Q}{9}=\dfrac{\sin 45^{\circ}}{7}$
$\sin Q=\dfrac{9\sin 45^{\circ}}{7}$
$Q=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{9\sin 45^{\circ}}{7}\right)$
$=65.39^{\circ}$
The obtuse partner is $180^{\circ}-65.39^{\circ}=114.61^{\circ}$; both are valid since $114.61^{\circ}+45^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$.
**Case 1** $Q=65.39^{\circ}$: $\angle R=180^{\circ}-45^{\circ}-65.39^{\circ}=69.61^{\circ}$.
$r=\dfrac{7\sin 69.61^{\circ}}{\sin 45^{\circ}}=9.28$
**Case 2** $Q=114.61^{\circ}$: $\angle R=180^{\circ}-45^{\circ}-114.61^{\circ}=20.39^{\circ}$.
$r=\dfrac{7\sin 20.39^{\circ}}{\sin 45^{\circ}}=3.45$

mastery.question_text: In triangle $ABC$, $a=13$ is opposite $\angle A=54^{\circ}$ and $b=7$ is opposite $\angle B$. Find $\angle B$, then find $\angle C$ and side $c$, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\sin B}{7}=\dfrac{\sin 54^{\circ}}{13}$
$\sin B=\dfrac{7\sin 54^{\circ}}{13}$
$B=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{7\sin 54^{\circ}}{13}\right)$
$=25.83^{\circ}$
The obtuse partner $180^{\circ}-25.83^{\circ}=154.17^{\circ}$ gives a sum over $180^{\circ}$ with $\angle A$, so it is rejected; $\angle B=25.83^{\circ}$.
$\angle C=180^{\circ}-54^{\circ}-25.83^{\circ}=100.17^{\circ}$
$c=\dfrac{13\sin 100.17^{\circ}}{\sin 54^{\circ}}=15.82$

mastery.question_text: In triangle $ABC$, $a=6$ is opposite $\angle A=35^{\circ}$ and $b=10$ is opposite $\angle B$. First decide how many triangles are possible by comparing $b\sin A$ with $a$, then find all possible sizes of $\angle B$, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
$b\sin A=10\sin 35^{\circ}=5.74$
Since $b\sin A<a<b$ (that is $5.74<6<10$), **two** triangles are possible.
$\dfrac{\sin B}{10}=\dfrac{\sin 35^{\circ}}{6}$
$\sin B=\dfrac{10\sin 35^{\circ}}{6}$
$B=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{10\sin 35^{\circ}}{6}\right)$
$=72.93^{\circ}$
The obtuse partner is $180^{\circ}-72.93^{\circ}=107.07^{\circ}$; both are valid since $107.07^{\circ}+35^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$.
$\angle B=72.93^{\circ}$ or $107.07^{\circ}$
